author: Autodesk
description: An aero grah producing a ground mist simulation, with adaptivity for low-res pre-roll.
documentation:
## Ground Mist Graph

### What it does

This graph uses aero to create a dynamic ground mist simulation

### Inputs and outputs 

Inputs for this graph are the ground mesh geometry from which mist will be emitted, which may also be used as collision geo.  The output is the resulting aero mist volume.

### Useful information

- The ground mist effect is accomplished by emitting fog very slowly and gradually.  Variations are used at sourcing time for both `fog_density` and `temperature`, keeping the max values low for both.  You don't want temperatures much higher than the `ambient temperature` as that will make the mist rise too quickly.  The more vertices on the sourcing geo, the finer the random variations for fog and temperature will be, thus producing more detail.  Style is smooth to maintain a ghostly look, using vorticity for added detail in denser areas.

- The behavior of ground mist works best at larger scene scales.  

- Performance is directly related to the `fluid detail size` on the source air node.  Since this effect is most likely to occur over large geometries, leveraging adaptivity with bounds is a good idea. In this graph, two bounding boxes are set up.  The first, which sets the resolution at half of what's specified in the source, serves to enable a low resolution pre-roll for teh first 24 frames.  Then, a second animated bounding box descends to bring the resolution back up to base. 

### Example scene

- The example scenes puts this effect in context by providing a landscape for the mist.  Portions of the scene geometry have been extracted to be used as sources.  The scene also leverages the ability of vary_source_property node to reference color per vertex maps from Maya.  In this case, not only is the fog density randomized at sourcing time, but it is also masked using a CPV map painted on the source geo. Finally, performance is optimized by doing a low resolution pre roll, and then increasing the resolution.  This accomplished by animating resolution bounding boxes plugged into the adaptivity node.

_notes.text:
Bounded adaptivity is enabled. Two bounding boxes are used. The

"half" bounding box sets resolution at half of what's specified in the source, and serves as a low-res pre-roll for 24 frames. The base resolution box then comes in to bring the resolution back up.
Add the same geo as the source with an offset for the mist to collide with. This is especially useful if additional collisions are added for objects passing trhhough the mist
These influences are the minimum for a ground mist effect, however, adding wind and turbulence can elevate the results.

_backdrops.title: This animates the position of the base resolution box
Using strands to draw the bounding boxes
